title: localinstall's 0059 FORWARD arm went red on WSL 2: the publish's stamp read a clean fixture source as dirty after its gate had read it committed, cause unknown
body:
The 0.1.19 cut's candidate CI went red on WSL 2 on one arm alone (run 41348944891, job 124974719427, `not ok 1566`, tests/unit/localinstall.bats:973, "0059: vendor reads FORWARD through an install"). `assert_output_contains "direction         forward --"` failed: vendor printed `vendored from 76c138bc... +dirty -- THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT` and `direction unknown`. The same arm was green in the first cut's WSL 2 run the same evening (run 41342983331, job 124956747963, `ok 1566`), on the same test code, the same WSL kernel (6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), Ubuntu 26.04.1 and git inside WSL (2.53.0-1ubuntu1.1). Only the Windows host image differed (20261021.278.1, then 20261030.294.1). It was green on Ubuntu in both runs, on macOS, on kovacs (Ubuntu 26.04, git 2.56) and on rhadamanth. WSL blocks nothing by design (tests.yml leaves it out of Test Summary's needs; AC-6.3: read job by job and fixed or filed), so the cut shipped 0.1.19 on Test Summary's green.

The `+dirty` was written by the first publish. consumer_of_install vendors the consumer and then upgrades it from the install, and that upgrade forwards the install's own stamp verbatim, so the consumer's `vendored from` line is the first publish's `source_commit`. In that one `install` command, publish_gate (lib/install) asked seam_state_of, through tree_dirty_paths, whether devbin's half of the source was committed, and got `committed`: otherwise the publish would have refused and the arm's `assert_success` after it would have failed. publish_install then copied from the source and wrote the manifest, whose source_commit_of asked seam_state_of the same question and got something else. Nothing devbin or the arm does writes to the source between the two reads, so the second read misread a clean tree. It erred safe: the stamp said less than the truth, never more.

Which answer the second read got is not in the log. source_commit_of writes `+dirty` for each of four: DIRTY (a line from git status), not tracked (an ignored file, or a symlink in the seam), not watched (an assume-unchanged or skip-worktree mark), and UNREADABLE (a seam path missing, or find, git status or git ls-files failing). The arm prints vendor's output alone.

The suspect this issue first named does not hold on WSL's git. mkdevsrc, commit_seam and ship_in_source (tests/lib/test_helper.bash) commit without `-c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0`, so each fixture commit starts a detached `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach` (traced under git 2.56). But the repacking maintenance 0233 caught is git's default only from git 2.54 (its release notes: "git maintenance" starts using the "geometric" strategy by default), and the WSL job runs git 2.53. There, an auto run with no maintenance config runs the gc task alone, and `gc --auto` leaves a repository this small alone. The job's only git config is a global safe.directory, which the suite's emptied global config never reads. So on WSL the background maintenance most likely wrote nothing under the fixture, and turning it off in those helpers is not expected to change this arm. That rests on git's release notes and documented defaults, not on a trace under git 2.53. CI's Ubuntu and macOS jobs ran git 2.56.0, whose release notes raise the geometric repack's loose-object threshold to gc --auto's, so they are not expected to repack a fixture this size either.

Status: cause unknown, intermittent. One red in the two WSL runs of this code, and none on any other platform. WSL blocks nothing by design. The 0.1.19 release and the real stamps are clean: the opt install records e532a0f6 with no `+dirty`, and none of the 37 devbin manifests in this machine's estates carries one. No fix is proposed: hv ruled on 2026-11-02 that this record is corrected and nothing else follows, no code and no run. What would place the cause is the answer the second read got, and the command that gave it.

Corrected 2026-11-02 03:52Z by date -u: the first text named the fixture commits' background maintenance as the suspect, and proposed turning it off as the fix.
